title: Quorum-driven zone placement with conditional fallback and residency gates
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Goal: Design and implement a quorum-driven placement strategy for regional and multi-zone Dedicated fleets that satisfies throughput guarantees while enforcing data residency constraints and offering deterministic conditional fallback behavior.

Context: Customers with committed capacity expect predictable throughput and capacity guarantees across regions. Current placement rules are primarily affinity/anti-affinity based and do not express a minimum-zone quorum or conditional fallback path when zones degrade. This leads to either overprovisioning or unexpected cross-region promotions that violate residency commitments.

Scope:
- Placement policy engine changes to support 'quorum intent' per dedicated pool (e.g., require 2-of-3 zones in a region). Pools will expose metadata: preferred_zones, min_zone_quorum, max_cross_region_spill (percentage).
- Autoscaler semantics: when one zone falls below healthy thresholds, autoscaler evaluates quorum impact and triggers either staggered redistribution within remaining zones or conditional fallback to a standby region subject to residency gates.
- Residency gates: explicit checks in the placement path that prevent cross-region fallback for pools with 'sovereign' residency unless an explicit emergency override is authorized.
- Throughput guarantees: map customer SLA tokens to zone-quota slices and track per-zone token burn. Implement fast-path admission control to preserve guaranteed throughput when operating at degraded quorum.
- Observability: new metrics and dashboards (quorum_status, per_zone_quota_usage, fallback_decision_reason, residency_violation_attempts) and traces for placement decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New placement API accepts min_zone_quorum and standby_region fields and persists policy.
2) Orchestrator can allocate a pool across zones satisfying quorum with deterministic allocation algorithm and deterministic tie-breakers.
3) Autoscaler triggers a 'quorum-maintain' plan that preserves throughput guarantees within remaining zones up to configured max_cross_region_spill before any cross-region fallback.
4) Residency gates block cross-region fallback when sovereignty=true; fallback path requires manual signed override and is audited.
5) Full e2e test harness simulating zone degradation to validate throughput SLAs, quota slicing, and fallback audit logs.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Quorum model adds complexity to allocation but gives predictable degradation semantics versus pure affinity.
- We will avoid automatic stateful migrations (live model copies) during fallback in first rollout; instead we will gracefully redirect new requests to fallback variants with documented eventual consistency.
- To keep latency SLOs, throughput guarantees in degraded quorum will prioritize reserved capacity and rate-limit non-reserved workloads.

Implementation notes:
- Placement policy stored in central config (control plane) and propagated via delta patches to fleet agents.
- Quorum evaluation executed in two phases: preflight (before allocation) and live re-eval (on health changes). Both must be idempotent.
- Admission control hooks added to serving runtime to enforce per-zone quota slices.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind org opt-in; internal teams only.
2) Deploy placement engine changes to staging, run chaos scenarios (zone flaps) against canary dedicated pools.
3) Enable autoscaler logic for non-sovereign pools first, observe metrics for 2 weeks.
4) Gradually enable residency gate enforcement for customers who requested sovereign enforcement.

Docs and artifacts: design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/quorum-placement-2026 (internal)
Prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/placemeNT/quorum-experiment
Relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2891

Test plan: unit tests for placement allocator, integration tests with autoscaler simulator, e2e with synthetic traffic replay preserving token-level SLA assertions.
